content:
The image shows a very young soybean seedling at/just above the soil surface. Key observations:
- Seedling is collapsed and unable to stand
- Tissue is brown, soft-looking, and deteriorated
- Cotyledons appear rotted and collapsed, not firm
- The hypocotyl region at the soil line shows discolored, soft tissue
- No firm dry canker visible (rules out Rhizoctonia)
- No distinct chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending upward (rules out Phytophthora)
- The soft, collapsed, brown rot at the seedling emergence point is consistent with pre/post-emergence damping off

This pattern — soft, water-soaked collapse of the seedling at or near the soil line with rotted tissue — is the hallmark of **Pythium damping off**.
